official.deadline_note: TU Delft warns that missing the scholarship deadline means the scholarship application will not be reviewed; applicants should apply before whichever deadline falls first - the MSc programme application deadline or the scholarship deadline.
official.status_note: The official TU Delft scholarships page currently publishes the 1 December 2026 (23:59 CET) scholarship deadline and an end-of-March 2027 notification date, i.e. the round for 2027 entry is open.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Awarded students will receive full tuition fees per year for a TU Delft MSc programme based on the Statutory or Institutional rate, according to the registered nationality, AND contribution for the living expenses.
benefits: Full tuition fees for the first year for a TU Delft MSc programme (based on the statutory fee or institutional rate, according to the registered nationality)
A monthly contribution towards living expenses for 24 months, as set out in the award letter
A two-year scholarship of approx. EUR 60,000 for non-EU students and approx. EUR 28,000 for EU students (Delft University Fund)
A minimum of 16 scholarships available every year, 2 per faculty
eligibility: Excellent international applicant (conditionally) admitted to one of the 2-year regular TU Delft MSc programmes (not an International Joint Education Programme)

Excellent academic results in previous study programme(s), which must be relevant to the Master's programme applied for; as an indication, amongst the top 10% of graduates (proof of ranking is not required)
You have submitted a complete MSc application before the scholarship deadline
Not eligible: TU Delft bachelor's students; international students who obtained their bachelor's degree at a Dutch university; students who have already started their MSc studies at TU Delft
Applicants must not be older than 35 years at the start of the first academic year (1 September)
requirements: A complete MSc application (Diploma, Transcript, English language certificate, Motivation letter, CV, Proof of Identity) uploaded before the deadline
A Scholarship Application Form (SAF) submitted at the same time as the MSc application
One reference letter (two references uploaded as one PDF)
The English language test must be included with the MSc application before the scholarship deadline (exempt applicants excepted)
A CGPA of at least 75% of the scale maximum to be admissible, unless country-specific CGPA requirements apply
documents: One reference letter (if two, combined into a single PDF)
selection_criteria: A positive admission assessment by the TU Delft admission office (conditional admission also counts)
Final selection made by TU Delft faculty selection committees after admission
Excellent academic results in a previous study programme relevant to the chosen MSc programme, with top 10% standing as the competitiveness indicator
Second-year allowances are conditional on completing at least 48 ECTS out of 60 in the first academic year
coverage: Full tuition fees for a TU Delft MSc programme, based on the statutory fee or institutional rate according to the registered nationality
A fixed monthly contribution towards living expenses, indicated in the scholarship contract, paid for 24 months
The fund publishes the two-year package as approx. EUR 60,000 for non-EU students and approx. EUR 28,000 for EU students
Flight costs and accommodation are not covered: flight tickets must be arranged and paid by the student and accommodation is at the student's own cost, with no extra allowance
application_method: Complete your MSc application through TU Delft's official application procedure
Upload the Scholarship Application Form with the MSc application
Upload one reference letter (two references as a single PDF)
Upload the English language certificate with the MSc application before the scholarship deadline
official.application_route: Apply through the regular TU Delft MSc application and upload the Scholarship Application Form, one reference letter and the English certificate alongside it - there is no separate scholarship portal.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to excellent international applicants; the tuition rate and scholarship value depend on registered nationality (EU vs non-EU). A bachelor's degree from a Dutch university makes an international applicant ineligible, and dual EU/non-EU nationals cannot apply as EU citizens to be considered for a non-EU scholarship amount.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Available for all TU Delft regular 2-year MSc programmes taught solely at TU Delft (not International Joint Education Programmes). Excluded programmes: Metropolitan Analysis, Design and Engineering; Applied Geophysics; The Berlage Post-master; Industrial Ecology; Geographical Information Management and Applications.
official.duration: Two years (24 months); financial extensions beyond the 2-year period are not supported
official.description: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships, financed by the legacy of Justus and Louise van Effen, give excellent international master students the opportunity to obtain their engineering degree at TU Delft. The two-year scholarship covers the full tuition fees and a contribution to living expenses, with a minimum of 16 scholarships available every year, 2 per faculty.
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic: overall 7.0 with minimum 6.5 per section (One Skill Retake accepted); TOEFL iBT: certificates issued from 21 January 2026 - overall 5 with minimum 4.5 per section, older certificates - overall 100 with minimum 22 per section; Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency: overall 185. Scores must be from a single test no older than two years and a verification/appointment/TRF number is required. Exempt: nationals of, or bachelor's graduates from, Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or the USA (overseas branches of these universities and English-taught degrees elsewhere do not qualify).

applicant_utility.summary: This is TU Delft's flagship MSc funding route: at least 16 full awards, two per faculty, each bundling full tuition with a monthly living contribution across the two years of a regular master's. Your single application act is to upload the Scholarship Application Form, a reference letter and an English test alongside a complete MSc application before 1 December 2026 - there is no separate scholarship portal and nothing can be added afterwards. Selection happens only after you are (conditionally) admitted, with faculty committees choosing winners and emailing them by end of March 2027; silence means unsuccessful. Budget separately for flights, rent and the first weeks of living costs before the September-October first payment.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-10% graduates from outside the Dutch university system who want a two-year TU Delft MSc funded and can submit a complete application in one go by 1 December.
application_readiness_checklist: Book IELTS/TOEFL months ahead and keep the TRF/appointment number - the certificate must be uploaded with the application and cannot follow later
Check which deadline falls first: your MSc programme deadline can precede the 1 December scholarship deadline
Prepare the Scholarship Application Form early and merge two reference letters into one PDF
Confirm your bachelor degree is relevant to the target MSc - committees weigh relevance heavily
Plan finances for flights, housing and September-October living costs before the first monthly payment
Verify your programme is not on the excluded list and check your EU/non-EU nationality classification
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete MSc application by the 1 December deadline - no later uploads, no reference letter added afterwards
Applying to an International Joint Education Programme or one of the five excluded MSc programmes
Holding a Dutch bachelor's degree or being a current/graduate TU Delft BSc student - automatically excluded
English test booked too late to have the certificate and verification number in the dossier
Age over 35 at the 1 September start of the first academic year
Assuming top-10% standing alone wins: without a relevant, coherent application file the dossier never reaches the faculty committee
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights and any travel, rent and accommodation above the monthly living allowance, the September-October living costs before the first payment, and any costs arising from study delay beyond the 24-month award period.
document_audit: Two reference letters must be combined into a single PDF upload - the dossier accepts one file
The Scholarship Application Form must ride the same submission as the MSc application, not arrive afterwards
The English certificate needs a TRF/appointment/verification number and an issue date within two years
Conditional admission still qualifies, but a confirmation statement must be submitted before the award is made official if selected
Diploma, transcript, motivation letter, CV and proof of identity must all be in place before the deadline
alerts: Age trap: you must be 35 or younger at the 1 September start of the first academic year
Dual EU/non-EU nationals cannot apply as EU citizens for the non-EU amount - nationality drives both eligibility and value
The award cannot be combined with any other partial or full scholarship funding
Second-year funding depends on 48 of 60 ECTS in year one, and there is no extension beyond 24 months
Tuition must be paid in full first if you have not yet been awarded - refunds occur only after the award is granted
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one complete MSc application through TU Delft's application system with the SAF, reference letter and English certificate attached, wait for the admission decision, and let the faculty selection committee consider you for the award - winners are notified by email by end of March 2027.
